newsitem.title: USA: Police believe murderer died in ValuJet crash.
newsitem.headline: Police believe murderer died in ValuJet crash.

text.p: A woman who stabbed and strangled a friend during an argument over money was one of 110 people who died when ValuJet Flight 592 crashed in the Florida Everglades last year, police said Wednesday.
College Park police said they closed their investigation into the murder of Catherine Holmes after concluding she was killed by DelMarie Walker on March 25, 1996.
Walker died in the crash of ValuJet Flight 592 on May 11, 1996. Her body was never recovered.
"The case is closed," police Lt. Richard Chromi said. "We are closing this investigation with the death of the prime suspect."

When police interviewed Walker two days after the murder, she had unexplained cuts on her hands and arm and was missing patches of hair on her head. She denied involvement in the crime and gave police hair and fingerprint samples but refused to give a blood sample that could have been compared to blood stains in the victim's apartment.

By the time the state crime lab completed its analysis of the hair and fingerprint evidence six months later, Walker had died in the crash, Chromi said. "We have her hairs in the hands of the victim. We have three fingerprints matched straight to the suspect" in the victim's bathroom, he said.

Holmes was found stabbed, bound and strangled in her ransacked apartment in the Atlanta suburb. There was no evidence of forcible entry. Police said she had told many friends that she had recently received a large amount of cash.
